title: Community services
description: Everything this setup runs for other people: the obfs4 and WebTunnel Tor bridges and the NTP Pool server on the A1, the Snowflake proxy, Psiphon Conduit and Kiwix seeding on the NAS. Counters reset when a container restarts; rate() and increase() absorb that.

panels.title: Status
panels.description: UP = the scrape answers. Conduit also needs a live Psiphon broker connection (conduit_is_live), NTP a working chrony command socket (chrony_up). Kiwix seeding is the qBittorrent exporter; whether peers can connect in is the 'Incoming port' tile further down.

panels.title: Bridge connections, last 24h
panels.description: User connections the obfs4 and WebTunnel transports handed to Tor in the last 24 h. A Tor client reconnects several times a day, so this counts connections, not people. Tor exports no gauge of users connected now: its state="opened" series for these connections never decreases. Unique users per day are in the bridge's stats/bridge-stats file.

panels.title: Conduit clients now
panels.description: Psiphon clients connected to the station right now (conduit_connected_clients). Capped by --max-common-clients.

panels.title: NTP queries / s
panels.description: NTP requests chrony received over the last 5 minutes. Stays near zero until the NTP Pool starts handing the server out (score above 10), and scales with the net speed set on manage.ntppool.org.

panels.title: Kiwix peers downloading
panels.description: Leechers connected to the Kiwix torrents (qBittorrent num_leechs): peers still downloading a ZIM file, the ones an upload from here helps.

panels.title: Traffic carried, selected range

targets.expr: (sum(increase(tor_relay_traffic_bytes[$__range])) or vector(0)) + ((sum(increase(tor_snowflake_proxy_traffic_inbound_bytes_total[$__range])) + sum(increase(tor_snowflake_proxy_traffic_outbound_bytes_total[$__range]))) * 1000 or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(conduit_bytes_uploaded[$__range])) + sum(increase(conduit_bytes_downloaded[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(qbittorrent_torrent_total_uploaded_bytes{name=~".+\\.zim"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + ((sum(increase(chrony_serverstats_ntp_packets_received_total[$__range])) * 2 - sum(increase(chrony_serverstats_ntp_packets_dropped_total[$__range]))) * 76 or vector(0))

panels.description: The five bars below added up. A service with no data in the range counts as zero instead of blanking the total.

panels.title: Traffic carried per service, selected range
panels.description: Both directions for the relays (Tor bridges read + written, Snowflake in + out, Conduit up + down) and for NTP (queries in + replies out); upload only for Kiwix, since the download is fetching the files for ourselves. chrony counts packets, not bytes, so NTP is derived: 76 B per packet (48 B NTP + 8 UDP + 20 IPv4) and one reply per query that ratelimit did not drop.

panels.title: Throughput per service
panels.description: Stacked. Tor bridges and NTP ride the A1's Oracle egress; Snowflake, Conduit and Kiwix all share the home uplink, so their stack is what remote streaming competes with. Snowflake is an hourly average: the proxy updates its traffic counters once an hour. NTP is derived from its packet counters at 76 B per packet.

panels.title: Tor bridges (A1) — details in Tor — Bridges & Snowflake
Bridge connections per hour
panels.description: New user connections per bridge, per rolling hour (connections, not people). Bridges are handed out by rdsys, so a new one sits near zero for days to weeks before it is distributed.

panels.title: Bridge throughput
panels.description: Bytes written (egress, what Oracle bills). Read is within a few percent of it for a bridge.

panels.title: Egress this month vs cap
panels.description: Each bridge has AccountingMax 1 TBytes (egress, month starting on the 1st) and hibernates at it. Orange at 80 %, red at 95 %. The month starts at 00:00 in the dashboard's time zone, Tor's at 00:00 UTC.

panels.title: Snowflake clients per hour
panels.description: Client connections handed to this proxy by the Snowflake broker, per rolling hour. No client cap is set: -capacity deadlocks the proxy.

panels.title: Snowflake throughput
panels.description: Hourly average. The proxy adds to its traffic counters once an hour, when it logs its summary, so a shorter rate() window turns each update into a spike. The proxy exports kilobytes, hence * 1000.

panels.title: Snowflake clients by country, selected range
panels.description: Top 10 by client country (ISO code) as the proxy reports it.

panels.title: Conduit clients
panels.description: Connected clients against --max-common-clients. Connecting = WebRTC handshakes in progress.

panels.title: Conduit throughput
panels.description: Directions as Conduit names them. The dashed line is --bandwidth (10 Mbps). The counters restart with the container; rate() absorbs that.

panels.title: Conduit clients by region, now
panels.description: Client region (ISO code) as the Psiphon broker reports it.

panels.title: Conduit traffic by region, selected range
NTP queries
panels.description: chronyc serverstats. Dropped = a client polling faster than the ratelimit allows; a few percent is normal pool traffic, a sudden climb is someone hammering the server.

panels.title: Clock offset
panels.description: How far chrony's estimate of true time is from its own clock. chronyd runs with -x and never steers the host clock, so this is the quality of the time it serves. The pool's monitors drop the score when it goes past about 75 ms; expect well under 1 ms.

panels.title: Upstream reachability
panels.description: Share of the last 8 polls each upstream answered. 169.254.169.254 is Oracle's link-local server; the others are ptbtime1-3.ptb.de and time.cloudflare.com (addresses, since DNS lookups are off).

panels.title: NTP totals
panels.description: The pool's own view (score, monitors) is at https://www.ntppool.org/scores/198.51.100.20.

panels.title: NTP bandwidth
panels.description: Derived, not measured: chrony exposes packet counts only. Every packet is 76 B on the wire (48 B NTP payload + 8 UDP + 20 IPv4 — the server has no IPv6 and no NTS, so the payload never varies), and one reply leaves per query that ratelimit did not drop. Ethernet framing (18 B per frame) is not counted, and neither is the query traffic to our own upstreams, which is a packet every few minutes.

panels.title: NTP data, selected range
panels.description: Same 76 B per packet as the panel on the left. Out is what counts against the A1's Oracle egress budget (10 TB/month, shared with the bridges and Matrix); a day of pool traffic is well under a gigabyte of it.

panels.title: Upload
panels.description: Kiwix = the .zim torrents kiwix-seed.sh manages. All torrents = qBittorrent's whole upload, for scale. Both leave the house through ProtonVPN on the home uplink.

panels.title: Kiwix peers
panels.description: Peers connected to the Kiwix torrents right now. Without a forwarded port only peers that accept incoming connections show up here.

panels.title: Incoming port
panels.description: qBittorrent's connection status. FIREWALLED = no incoming peer has connected, usually because the ProtonVPN forwarded port did not reach qBittorrent: see docs/services/downloads.md → Common failures.

panels.title: Torrents complete
panels.description: Kiwix torrents fully downloaded (seeding) out of all Kiwix torrents.

panels.title: On disk
panels.description: Downloaded part of the Kiwix files. kiwix-seed.sh budgets 300 GB (old and new month overlap while a new file downloads).

panels.title: Kiwix torrents
panels.description: One row per .zim torrent. Uploaded, total is qBittorrent's all-time figure for that torrent; a new month's file starts again at zero.
